name: Motor Driven Cycle
description: A light motorcycle whose motor produces no more than 5 brake horsepower (3,750 W); the term also takes in every moped. An electric two- or three-wheeler over the moped's 2 brake horsepower or 30 mph but within 5 brake horsepower lands here, and is otherwise ridden and registered as a motorcycle.

restrictions.rule: A motorcycle: a seat or saddle, and no more than three wheels on the ground
Its motor produces no more than 5 brake horsepower (3,750 W); one over that is a full motorcycle
One over 2 brake horsepower (1,500 W), or able to go faster than 30 mph, is a motor driven cycle rather than a moped
Riders need a Class M license, issued at 17 or older
A Class M instruction permit is available at 17, or at 16 after a driver education course, and isn't valid with a passenger, on a limited-access highway or at night
Riders and passengers must wear a helmet meeting the commissioner of public safety's standards, and eye protection unless it has a windshield
Registered and plated like any motorcycle, with the liability insurance required of a motor vehicle
Headlights and taillights must be on at all times
Entitled to a full lane; no passing in the same lane or riding between lanes, and no more than two abreast
